findings.location: sections/concise/10-commentary.tex line 293 ('The medieval commentators on the Mass read these chants as one sequence.'), and line 444 ('The real disagreements among the Fathers lie within the interpretations')
findings.problem: Compression has dropped a qualification and widened the claim. The expansive study says 'The medieval commentators on the Mass who expound these four chants read them as one sequence' (sections/40-already-and-awaited.tex lines 188-189). Its evidence is three commentators. research/scope.md section 3 and section 6 record that the commentary-work-index formulary query lists none for this Mass. Only Rupert, De div. off. XII.23, Sicard, Mitrale VIII.23, and Durandus, Rationale VI.140, were read, and Durandus's Joseph is Rupert's. Amalarius, Honorius, Beleth and Innocent III were not searched, and Schuster III was not re-read. Without the restrictive clause, the concise sentence presents the three that follow as examples of what medieval Mass commentators generally did. No record supports that consensus. It is a new source-dependent claim and a lost qualification that affects truth, both of which the concise study's contract forbids ('Qualifications that affect truth survive compression. Introduce no new source-dependent claim'), and the 1962 profile forbids implying consensus. This is not settled prose: this round's repair of SYN-007(c) rewrote the same paragraph two sentences later. The commentators' own readings are reported correctly. Checked at Rupert, PL 170 OCR (ia-djvu-ocr-2e2ca850) lines 23697-23790: the remnant of Israel saved in fine mundi, the thanks of the Gradual 'captivitate animarum', and the Communion's 'Nolite timere'. Checked at Sicard, PL 213 OCR (ia-djvu-ocr-ea9fd813) lines 29951-29975: Israelis reliquiae in the time of Antichrist, and the Communion's 'certificat de salute'. The only defect is the breadth of the claim. The closing sentence at line 444 drops 'cited here' from the expansive's 'The real disagreements among the Fathers cited here' (sections/50-comparison.tex line 344) in the same way. In context it is less likely to mislead, but two words restore it.
findings.required_result: Restrict the sentence to the commentators actually read. For example: 'Three medieval commentators on the Mass who expound these chants read them as one sequence.' or 'The medieval commentators on the Mass who expound these four chants read them as one sequence.' At line 444: 'The real disagreements among the Fathers cited here lie within the interpretations, over what the seed, the leaven and the measures are.'

findings.location: sections/concise/10-commentary.tex lines 210-211 ('Paul had reasoned in their synagogue that "the Christ was to suffer and to rise again from the dead" (Acts 17:3), the belief by which, Ambrose says, faith is pressed.')
findings.problem: This sentence was rewritten this round under SYN-005. It now has Ambrose name the whole belief of Acts 17:3, suffering and rising, as what presses faith. At Exp. in Lucam VII.181 (tracked Wikisource artifact book-7-html-895ee72a) he says 'Premitur fides, cum crucifixum credimus Christum'. He then goes straight on: 'Et quia docuit premere fidem, docuit et levare, dicens: Nunc enim crucifixum iam non novimus Christum' (2 Cor 5:16). For him the cross presses faith and the risen Christ lifts it, so the rising belongs to the other motion. The expansive study (sections/20-crushed-seed.tex lines 208-215) keeps Ambrose to faith pressed by belief in the crucified, and states the link to Thessalonica as the study's own ('On Ambrose's account, then'). The over-reach is one clause carried inside a quotation, and the next sentence's conclusion still holds, so this is advisory.
findings.required_result: Credit Ambrose only with the crucified. For example: 'Paul had reasoned in their synagogue that "the Christ was to suffer" (Acts 17:3), and Ambrose says that faith is pressed when we believe in Christ crucified.'

findings.location: sections/20-crushed-seed.tex lines 175-191 (expansive study: the citation run on Chrysostom's homilies on First Thessalonians)

It then gives the affliction-and-joy sentence and the imitators of the Lord, both from Homily 1 (NPNF I.13, ccel-npnf113-text-54274dd9, lines 29262-29271). This stage cannot repair it; the concise study now cites Homily 1 correctly.

summary: Reviewed the concise study synthesis.tex of the Claude 1962 leaf 67-resumed-sixth-after-epiphany as derive-synthesis iteration 1 left it; every sealed REVIEW_INPUTS file was re-hashed and matched the packet. Read cold, the concise prose alone gives three distinct answers: (1) the seed (the Lord for Hilary, faith and Christ for Ambrose) gives its strength when crushed, so the small grows great through pressure, seen in a church pressed first and then heard of everywhere; (2) the leaven is love (Augustine, Bede) or the teaching that commands it (Jerome, Ambrose), hidden in the whole person and working inward until the whole is changed, finished in no one in this life; (3) deliverance is sung as done because what God foretells is as certain as the past (Augustine) and its cause, sin, is removed now (Aquinas), while his people pray for what is promised (Jerome) and the whole is leavened when Christ comes (Chrysologus). These match the expansive study's comparison, and within each question the authors of the different interpretations meet at the shared text. Checked at their loci in tracked texts (hashes matched): Ambrose, Exp. in Lucam VII.176-194; Chrysostom, Hom. in Mt. 46.2-3, 47.1, 67.2 and Hom. in 1 Thess. 1-2 (NPNF); Augustine, En. in Ps. 43.1, 43.6-7, 84.2-4 and 77.1-2 (NPNF) and Quaest. Ev. I.11-12; Hilary, In Mt. 13.4-6 and Tract. in Ps. 129.2-3 (PL 9 OCR); Chrysologus, Sermo 98-99 (PL 52 OCR); Bede, In Marcum on 11:25; Aquinas, Super Mt. c. 13 (1745 OCR); Rupert XII.23; Sicard VIII.23; Vulgate Mt 7:7 and Jn 16:24 with Jerome's own Petite, et accipietis at PL 24 OCR line 17182 (so the Mt 7:7 locus is his form, not an error). Remote files fetched and matched to their registered SHA-256: Bede, In Lucam (116db0ca..., on 13:19 and 13:21), Aquinas c1t.html (fe77f056...) and cps41.html (7879ef13...). Jerome's PL 26 page images were not re-read; his wording follows research/scope.md. Every repair claimed for SYN-001 to SYN-007 was verified in the text. Page-2 lookup on the generated table: Communion, Mark 11:24, is one row whose occurrence is 'Jesus teaches faith and prayer; Bethany to Jerusalem, before the Passion', dated A.D. 29 (derived; Maas's chronology), with composition 'Mark; Rome traditionally', proposals A.D. 38-70; Epistle, 1 Thess 1:2-10, is 'First Thessalonians; Corinth to Thessalonica', proposals A.D. 52-54. Each pairing was read across one row without entering another column's text, so the page is usable. Physical evidence: an independent build (make doc with BUILD_ROOT in this review's scratch) gave 12 pages, no overfull or underfull box, and settled zref markers with the inventory, overview and four sense rows on page 1, the chronology on page 2, the themes on pages 3-4 (page 4 about 85 per cent filled) and the commentary from page 5; PDF SHA-256 501eb5cd21c6dbb61c9c5759c61eb6b2c954d8a42c7f69dbc7fdfcd34cd84fe7, with an uncommitted-sources revision line. This is not a print acceptance. Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED on one blocking finding, SYN-009, where compression turns the study's statement about the three Mass commentators it read into a statement about medieval Mass commentators generally. SYN-010 is a new advisory, and SYN-008 is carried forward for the study owner.
